answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashable identity bond: every agent locks collateral before it may mine or grade, and any account caught double-voting or colluding forfeits that stake to honest reporters. Splitting into a thousand fake agents therefore needs a thousand separate bonds. Rewards per identity are capped, so attacker cost rises linearly with the number of identities while payoff stays flat. At dawn a fresh ridge of throwaway accounts looks cheap, but the rising tide of forfeited bonds makes the flood a net loss.
